chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Aban, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning a man who confessed against himself to a hadd punishment, then later denied it.

He عليه السلام said: “If he confesses against himself before the Imam that he stole, then later denies it, his hand is cut off, even if he is unwilling. And if he confesses against himself that he drank wine or made a false accusation, then flog him with eighty lashes.”
I said: If he confesses against himself to a hadd punishment in which stoning is required, would you stone him? He عليه السلام said: “No, but I would administer the hadd to him.”

key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: stoning as a legal penalty in certain hadd cases
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the legitimate authority before whom the confession is made
key_terms.بِحَدٍّ: a punishable offense carrying a fixed legal penalty
key_terms.بِفِرْيَةٍ: with false accusation or slanderous allegation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone confesses to a hadd offense and then later denies it?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses legal rulings concerning a person who confesses to a hadd offense and then retracts the confession. It distinguishes between theft, drinking wine, false accusation, and offenses involving rajm, indicating how the Imam عليه السلام would apply the prescribed hadd in each case.
